rows.prediction: Milwaukee Brewers to win World Series Game 2 at Tampa Bay. MLB.com records the Brewers taking Game 1 by a 10-1 margin, and OLBG's two recorded money-line tips both favour Milwaukee, who posted the best regular-season record in baseball. A Rays bullpen that was thumped for double-digit runs overnight faces another deep, flexible Brewers pitching staff. Selection: Brewers money line, with the one-run-game volatility of playoff baseball keeping confidence at medium rather than high.

rows.prediction: Afghanistan to beat Zimbabwe in the first T20 at Sharjah. Fifteen of sixteen OLBG tips back Afghanistan, and the event-page record shows them beating Zimbabwe by seven wickets in Friday's ODI final, with Rashid Khan taking three wickets and Farooqi removing both openers. Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Noor Ahmad strengthen a spin attack Zimbabwe's top order has already failed against. Selection: Afghanistan to win the match.

flags: Largest-sample cricket market on the board; OLBG commentary cites India's 2-0 series lead
rows.prediction: India to win the third T20 against New Zealand. This is the deepest market on the cricket card with 49 recorded tips, 35 of them on India, who already lead the series 2-0. OLBG commentary notes New Zealand's inconsistent batting, with Kane Williamson failing to convert starts, while India's top order and pace-bowling starts have controlled both games. The hosts must chase the game, which suits India's bowling changes. Selection: India to win the match.

rows.prediction: Pakistan to beat Sri Lanka in the tri-series ODI. Twenty-two of thirty-one OLBG tips favour Pakistan, who have won all three games in the tournament including a 37-run defeat of Sri Lanka. Salman Ali Agha made 107 in that meeting and Shaheen Afridi has seven wickets in the series, making the new-ball duel a stark mismatch on paper. Selection: Pakistan to win the match.

Ireland to beat Namibia in the third ODI. Twenty-two of thirty-two OLBG tips back the Irish, a clear majority on a 32-tip market, and the ICC fixture list confirms the decider. Ireland's greater depth in both the powerplay and the death overs has been the difference between these associate-plus sides across the series. Selection: Ireland to win the match, medium-high confidence given Namibia's improving home form.

rows.prediction: Oyonnax to beat Soyaux-Angouleme in Pro D2 round nine. The LNR table has Oyonnax sitting top of the division and hosting a fourth-placed challenger, with two of three OLBG tips also taking the home side. Oyonnax's set-piece and maul work has been the engine of their start, and travelling sides rarely leave their ground with anything. Selection: Oyonnax to win.

rows.prediction: Grenoble to win away at Beziers. The LNR standings frame this as the round's biggest mismatch on paper: third-placed Grenoble travel to a Beziers side anchored in 15th. Grenoble's backline tempo and dominant scrum have ground down lower-table teams all season, while Beziers have leaked points in the final quarter. Selection: Grenoble to win, with the single-tip OLBG market backed by the official table.

Narbonne's away discipline has cost them field position repeatedly. Selection: Montauban to win, medium confidence given the three-tip sample.

rows.prediction: Glasgow Warriors to beat the Lions at Scotstoun. The lone OLBG tip takes the home side, and Glasgow's abrasive defence and tempo on the artificial surface have historically made them formidable at home against travelling South African franchises jet-lagged from the trip north. The Lions carry physicality but have struggled to sustain it for eighty minutes on the road. Selection: Glasgow Warriors to win.
